value.name: Asha accepts guest status
value.description: Asha identifies herself as a guest, and the invitation is framed as entering without taking sides.
evidence: "Then come in as a guest and refuse to take sides."

value.name: Asha notices the house has been rearranged
value.description: Asha is surprised by the smell of stew, bread, and wood fire, and realizes the house now has a lit fireplace and moved furniture.
evidence: The house smelled of stew and of bread and of a wood fire, which surprised her, because she had not registered, on any of her previous visits, that the house had a working fireplace.

There was one, in the front parlor, and it was lit, and Daniel was sitting in front of it in an armchair that Asha recognized as having previously been in the back parlor, which suggested that some rearranging had been going on.

value.name: Daniel greets Asha warmly
value.description: Daniel stands when Asha enters and greets her by name, expressing that he is glad she came.
evidence: He stood up when she came in.

value.name: Daniel appears less tense
value.description: Asha observes that Daniel has relaxed somewhat, though some deeper tension remains and may never fully leave him.
evidence: He had lost a little of the tightness around his eyes. Not all of it.
Some of it, she suspected, would never leave, because some of it was older than this estate and older than his mother's death and older than the codicil

value.name: Asha senses Daniel may be accepted
value.description: Asha interprets Daniel's expression as tentative hope that he might be liked without having to earn it.
evidence: what had replaced it was something that looked, in the firelight, like a man who had begun, tentatively, to consider the possibility that he might be liked by the people in the room without having to earn it that evening.

value.name: Daniel serves Asha wine
value.description: Daniel pours Asha a glass of wine even though she did not bring any as instructed.
evidence: He poured her a glass of wine.
She had not brought any, as instructed.

value.name: Asha and Daniel converse casually
value.description: Asha and Daniel stand by the fire and talk about nothing in particular, marking a shift from their usual transactional conversations.
evidence: They stood by the fire and talked about nothing in particular, which was a thing she had not done with Daniel before, because every previous conversation with Daniel had been about something in particular, and the particular thing had usually been a thing he wanted from her.
